tagline: Delivering value through world-class utility performance and energy transition
hero_kpi_rationale: The utilities sector is highly capital-intensive, and capital expenditures are a key indicator of financial health and the ability to invest in the energy transition and distribution infrastructure.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Capital expenditures for infrastructure and equipment
kpis.description: Capital expenditures are essential to maintain and enhance infrastructure and equipment
kpis.signal: Increase in capital expenditures to support growth

kpis.name: Long-Term Debt
kpis.explanation: Consolidated long-term debt of the company
kpis.description: Long-term debt reflects financing of the major investment program in the energy transition

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash flow generated from operating activities
kpis.description: Operating cash flow is essential to fund company operations and investments
kpis.signal: Slight decrease in operating cash flow

kpis.name: Total PPA Purchase Obligations
kpis.explanation: Total contractual energy purchase commitments (Power Purchase Agreements) by CMS Energy over the full term of the contracts.
kpis.description: CMS Energy has contracted $16.98 Bn in energy purchases through PPAs, including $12.3 Bn beyond 2030. These commitments reflect structural reliance on long-term supply contracts.

kpis.name: Total Long-Term Debt Principal
kpis.explanation: Total principal amount of long-term debt of CMS Energy (before deductions for discounts and unamortized issuance costs).
kpis.description: CMS Energy's total long-term debt principal reaches $18.94 Bn at end-2025 versus $16.55 Bn at end-2024, driven by $3.46 Bn in new issuances in 2025. Growth reflects financing of the large-scale investment plan.

kpis.name: Long-Term Debt Issuances 2025
kpis.explanation: Total volume of new long-term debt issuances completed by CMS Energy during fiscal year 2025.
kpis.description: CMS Energy issued $3.46 Bn in new debt in 2025, including $2.11 Bn at the parent level (convertible notes, subordinated notes) and $1.13 Bn at Consumers (mortgage bonds). These issuances fund the ongoing investment program.

kpis.name: MCV PPA Annual Charges
kpis.explanation: Annual capacity and energy charges paid by Consumers Energy under the power purchase agreement with the MCV partnership (1,240 MW).
kpis.description: MCV PPA charges amount to $360 M in 2025 (vs $358 M in 2024 and $340 M in 2023), reflecting a slight increase. A new 10-year contract was signed in September 2025 for the post-2030 period, securing 1,240 MW of capacity.

kpis.name: Gain on Repurchase of Bonds Consumers
kpis.explanation: Pre-tax gain realized by CMS Energy upon repurchasing at a discount the mortgage bonds of its subsidiary Consumers Energy.
kpis.description: CMS Energy repurchased $184 M in principal of Consumers bonds for $109 M in cash in 2025, generating a pre-tax gain of $72 M (vs $110 M in 2024 on $404 M and $131 M in 2023 on $431 M). Repurchase volume is significantly declining.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $1.14 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four fiscal years reported.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.663 Bn in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Portion of net income distributed as dividends: 61.9% in the latest year.

risks.title: Regulatory Changes and Energy Compliance
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the Michigan 2023 Energy Law with ambitious targets: 50% renewable energy by 2030, 60% by 2035, 80% clean energy by 2035, and 100% by 2040. The energy storage mandate requires 2,500 MW at the state level, with 817 MW assigned to Consumers. Compliance is central for a regulated utility.

risks.title: Dependence on Regulatory Decisions
risks.score_rationale: The text details several cases where decisions by the MPSC and FERC are crucial, such as resource plan approvals, cost recovery for coal plants, and rate setting. Uncertainty surrounding these approvals and associated litigation indicates high risk.

risks.title: Risks Related to Energy Transition and Plant Closures
risks.score_rationale: The closure of coal plants (D.E. Karn in 2023, J.H. Campbell) and the acquisition of new capacity (energy storage, renewables) are major elements in the text. The language describes a multi-faceted strategy to meet targets, involving execution and cost risks.

risks.title: Litigation and Regulatory Challenges
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions several ongoing challenges regarding regulatory decisions and transactions. The language intensity is moderate, but the nature of the disputes is serious and could lead to delays and additional costs.

risks.title: Demand Volatility and Economic Conditions
risks.score_rationale: The text highlights that customer deliveries are seasonal and dependent on Michigan's economy, citing factors such as data center expansion and general economic trends. While outlook is positive, reliance on these factors remains a risk.

risks.title: Cost Management and Investment Recovery
risks.score_rationale: The document mentions the need to recover costs from retired plants, significant investments in energy storage and renewables ($25.8 Bn over 5 years for CMS Energy). Recovery of these costs depends on regulatory decisions and access to capital markets.

ai_positioning.summary: CMS Energy did not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
